A.explanation: $0.05 \text{ ms} = 0.05 \times 10^{-3} \text{ s} = 5.0 \times 10^{-5} \text{ s}$, which is 1000 times larger than the shortest interval.

B.explanation: $50 \text{ ns} = 50 \times 10^{-9} \text{ s} = 5.0 \times 10^{-8} \text{ s}$, which is smaller than all the other converted values.

C.explanation: $500\,000 \text{ ps} = 5 \times 10^{5} \times 10^{-12} \text{ s} = 5.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ s}$, which is 10 times larger than the shortest interval.

D.explanation: $0.5 \text{ }\mu\text{s} = 0.5 \times 10^{-6} \text{ s} = 5.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ s}$, equal to option C and 10 times larger than the shortest interval.

hints: Notice all four times use different SI prefixes: $\text{m}$, $\text{n}$, $\text{p}$ and $\mu$ attached to $\text{s}$, so you cannot compare the numbers 0.05, 50, 500000 and 0.5 directly.
Recall the prefix powers for time: $1 \text{ ms}=10^{-3} \text{ s}$, $1 \text{ }\mu\text{s}=10^{-6} \text{ s}$, $1 \text{ ns}=10^{-9} \text{ s}$ and $1 \text{ ps}=10^{-12} \text{ s}$.
Convert each interval to seconds or to nanoseconds, paying attention to the large $500\,000$ multiplier on the picosecond value, then order the four powers of ten.
walkthrough: Identify the given quantities: $0.05 \text{ ms}$, $50 \text{ ns}$, $500\,000 \text{ ps}$ and $0.5 \text{ }\mu\text{s}$. The rule is to express all times in the same base unit, the second.
Write each prefix as a power of ten: $\text{m}=10^{-3}$, $\mu=10^{-6}$, $\text{n}=10^{-9}$, $\text{p}=10^{-12}$.
Convert: $0.05 \text{ ms}=0.05 \times 10^{-3} \text{ s}=5.0 \times 10^{-5} \text{ s}$ and $50 \text{ ns}=50 \times 10^{-9} \text{ s}=5.0 \times 10^{-8} \text{ s}$.

Convert the other two: $500\,000 \text{ ps}=5.0 \times 10^{5} \times 10^{-12} \text{ s}=5.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ s}$ and $0.5 \text{ }\mu\text{s}=0.5 \times 10^{-6} \text{ s}=5.0 \times 10^{-7} \text{ s}$.
Compare in seconds: $5.0 \times 10^{-8} < 5.0 \times 10^{-7} < 5.0 \times 10^{-5}$. The smallest power of ten is $10^{-8} \text{ s}$ from the $50 \text{ ns}$ interval.
